schema.description: Example model of a theatre business: stages (venues) where programs (shows) are played by actors, and the individual events (performances) at which a program is played on a stage.

knot.description: Kind of parent-child relationship between two actors, such as biological or adoptive parent.
Professional level of an actor, describing experience and seniority, such as amateur, trained or professional.
Utilization expressed as a percentage (0-100) of the capacity of a stage that is in use.
Yes or No flag indicating whether a relationship is still ongoing or has ended.
Rating of how well an actor performs a part in a program, such as good, mediocre or bad.
Type of event, such as premiere, regular performance, rehearsal or gala.

anchor.description: A person. Persons who perform are also registered as actors.
A stage or venue where programs are played and events are held.

attribute.description: Name of the stage. Historized, since a stage may be renamed over time.
Geographic location of the stage as a geography point.
Average utilization of the stage capacity, recalculated over time.
Minimum utilization of the stage capacity required for a performance to take place.

anchor.description: An actor, a person who performs parts in programs and is cast in events.

attribute.description: Name of the actor, such as a stage name. Historized, since it may change over time.
Professional level of the actor, which may change as the actor gains experience.

anchor.description: A program, such as a play, show or concert, that can be played on stages.

attribute.description: Name or title of the program.
Running time of the program. Historized, since the program may be shortened or extended over time.

nexus.description: An event, a single performance of a program held at a stage at a specific date and time.

attribute.description: Date and time when the event took place.
Number of people in the audience at the event.
Revenue from ticket sales for the event.

role.description: The stage at which the event was held.
The program that was played at the event.
The type of the event.

tie.description: Marriage or domestic partnership between two actors. This is a one-to-one relationship, since an actor can have at most one partner at any point in time. History is never deleted, so the end of a partnership is recorded by changing its ongoing status to No.

role.description: One of the actors in the partnership.
The other actor in the partnership.
Whether the partnership is still ongoing (Yes) or has ended (No).

tie.description: Connects an actor to the person that the actor is. Every actor is a person, but not every person is an actor.

role.description: The actor.
The person who is the actor.

tie.description: The actors that were cast in an event, meaning those who performed at that performance.

role.description: The event the actor was cast in.
An actor cast in the event.

tie.description: Actors having a part in a program, along with a rating of how well they perform the part. Historized, since the rating may change over time.

role.description: The actor having a part in the program.
The program the actor has a part in.
The rating the actor got for the part.

tie.description: Programs that are currently playing at stages, meaning which stage is running which program. Historized over time.

role.description: The stage where the program is playing.
The program playing at the stage.

tie.description: Parent-child relationships between actors, along with the type of parental relationship.

role.description: The actor who is the parent.
The actor who is the child.
The type of parental relationship.

tie.description: The program content and stage location of an event, connecting each event to what was played and where. This deliberately repeats the wasHeldAt and wasPlayed roles of the Event nexus, to show that the same fact can be modeled either as nexus roles or as a tie.

role.description: The program that made up the content of the event.
The stage where the event was located.
The event.
